task.instruction: Find the article "What is climate change? A really simple guide" and use it to answer what human activities are causing climate change.

final_answer:
According to the BBC News article "What is climate change? A really simple guide" (page title; the headline reads "A really simple guide to climate change"), human activities are causing world temperatures to rise. The main cause is the widespread use of fossil fuels (coal, oil and gas) in homes, factories and transport systems.

Burning fossil fuels releases greenhouse gases, mostly carbon dioxide (CO2). The CO2 acts like a blanket and traps extra energy in the atmosphere near the Earth's surface, which heats the planet. Since the start of the Industrial Revolution, when humans began burning large amounts of fossil fuels, atmospheric CO2 has risen by more than 50%. The article says the CO2 from fossil fuels has a distinctive chemical fingerprint that matches the CO2 increasingly found in the atmosphere.

The article says natural causes can't explain the rapid warming of the last century. It cites the IPCC, which says the warming has been caused by human activities "without doubt". The article doesn't list other causes in this section. It mentions deforestation only in connection with the COP30 climate talks.

judge.rationale: The agent found the BBC article and answered with the article’s stated cause: widespread fossil fuel use in homes, factories and transport releasing CO2/greenhouse gases.
